A cheaper (or same-priced) plan is a downgrade: nothing is refunded or prorated, the member keeps the current plan until its period ends, and the new price is charged from the next period. What the subscription grants (a membership's classes) follows the plan when it takes effect. Only an active subscription not set to end, with no other change waiting. operations.name: subscription.coolOff
operations.description: End a subscription in its cooling-off period, for a full refund of what was paid in it (subscription.coolingOff says whether it may be, and what it owes). Ended at the payment provider now: nothing more is charged, and what it gives stops once the provider confirms. Then each order paid up to the end of the period, and between the ask and the end, is owed back in full, whatever was used; each waits for a person with orders:refund to approve it. The bookings ahead the membership paid for are cancelled as the business's. Refused for a plan with no cooling off, a membership moved over with a continuation offer, a member who has cooled off before, while nothing has been paid (a free trial: cancel instead), and after the period unless one was asked in it. An ask inside the period opens it for 7 days; any end in that time is the cooling off's, and at its deadline it lapses (the ordinary cancel works again). A signed-in customer ends their own (the one they pay for, a child's included) and asks again only inside the period; staff any, with subscriptions:manage, ask again until the deadline, and finish a lapsed one (only what was paid in the period is owed, once the provider confirms the membership ended). Each ask reads the provider first and is a new request to it; nothing is done twice. Refused while a cancel of it waits for a person at the payments gatekeeper. A person decides, never an AI assistant.
